A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fun3DU study and include the main paper and supplementary material. Text, equations, tables, and visual results can be matched reliably, including the identifiable label removal in v4 supplementary Figure 4.

before.justification: v1 reports original SceneFun3D evaluations, baseline comparisons, ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative results in the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark tables and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The four-stage pipeline, prompts, hierarchy selection, view scoring, and 3D aggregation remain unchanged. Calling the text-reasoning component an LLM corrects earlier VLM terminology; v1 already specifies Llama for this component in Section 4.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SceneFun3D functionality-segmentation task and retain both splits and the same qualitative scenarios. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: OpenMask3D, OpenIns3D, and LERF remain the evaluated baselines. Supplementary comparisons retain the same prompt variants and OpenIns3D configurations using Yolo-world or ODISE, with and without Snap.

E3.justification: The 30/200-scene splits, AP/AR/IoU metrics, model configurations, quantization, default 50 selected views, threshold 0.7, and baseline processing procedures remain unchanged. Revised captions clarify existing settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the architectural and view-score ablations, view-count and threshold sensitivity analyses, baseline prompt/rendering analyses, and supplementary success and failure cases. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Both retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 and supplementary Tables 1–3 retain their numerical entries. Fun3DU mIoU remains 15.2 on split0 and 11.5 on split1. The sensitivity curves, timing results, and qualitative findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), including polar coordinates, divergence scores, view ranking, and 3D aggregation, remain unchanged. The contextual-object wording is a conceptual clarification; no mathematical derivation, formal result, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: a first dedicated, training-free functionality-segmentation approach using pretrained models, a view-selection contribution, and superior performance over the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 broaden the contextual interpretation: O changes from a parent physically containing the functional object to an object containing or spatially related to it, and the prior becomes proximity rather than part membership. Existing failure analyses and future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promised future code release with a project-page link, adding concrete access information. The PDFs do not establish whether code is available there. Checkpoint links, hyperparameters, and A100 implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 36 main-paper and 12 supplementary references are retained. Research positioning relative to SceneFun3D, open-vocabulary segmentation, and vision-language models remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 standardizes LLM/VLM and parent/contextual terminology, makes local prose corrections, puts the third module before the fourth in the introduction, and adds acknowledgements. The section structure and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Main Figure 2 is relabeled and several captions are revised. Supplementary Figure 4 loses its task headings and method/ground-truth row labels while retaining the same images and scores, reducing readability. Table structures and the overall layout remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies the LLM/VLM roles and spatial-context interpretation and adds a project-page link. However, supplementary Figure 4 loses labels needed to interpret its comparisons. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these limited documentation benefits and the concrete loss of readability leave the net quality effect unclear.
